sources.governing_conditions_defaults_units_exce: Site analysis/local requirements govern; handbook is guidance, not a binding specification. The capture alternatives have geometry, erosion, access and maintenance conditions. A level spreader distributes concentrated flow; filter strips need suitable space and sheet flow. No handbook dimension is used in the final.
sources.checked_claim_and_assessment: Conditional inlet/approach review, pretreatment, underdrain distinction, design/as-built history, and the New York/Portland issue-fix examples are supported. Final uses the examples at a more general level than discovery/draft.
sources.applicability_limits: No local dimensions, grade, contributing area, intent, hydrology, cause or treatment performance established; no current errata assertion made. Published municipal examples are analogous evidence, not this site’s history.

sources.type_and_domain: official primary guidance or primary research record; urban stormwater/bioretention

sources.locator: Web-render L86–95 (typical issues), L109–164 (local context/construction/O&M), L170–178 (schedule), L200–212 (mulch/troubleshooting).
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_units_exce: The 48-hour check is semiannual after the first year, after rain with unfrozen ground; deep sumps may pond. First-year table refers to >0.5-inch storms during first six months. Troubleshooting lists possible sediment, pretreatment, debris and grading causes. These are contextual guidance, not a local diagnosis or universal threshold.
sources.checked_claim_and_assessment: Final correctly treats leaves/mulch/sediment and grading as competing leads, keeps 48 hours as an observation time, and defers governing drawdown criteria to the site partner. It does not prescribe table repairs.
sources.applicability_limits: Minnesota is not established as this site’s jurisdiction. Generic schedules cannot establish compliance, cause or permission. Native direct GET returned an anti-bot page; only independent web-render content is used as governing evidence.

sources.title: Alleviating compaction from construction activities
sources.released_version_or_commit: Living manual page; explicitly under review/revision (web-render L61); current commit not exposed
sources.type_and_domain: official primary guidance or primary research record; urban stormwater/bioretention
sources.reviewer_operation: independent retrieval and substantive inspection of specified governing passages; no field work or source-data reanalysis
sources.locator: Web-render L61–63; L103–133 (causes and identification); L145; L211; L222–241 (site dependence/mixed methods).
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_units_exce: Construction traffic, storage and stockpiling can compact soil; wet/clay soils are more susceptible. Ponding may indicate compaction but measurements have limits. Remediation is site-specific, and compaction may be intentional in some other construction applications.
sources.checked_claim_and_assessment: Treating the delivery as an unverified lead and avoiding an automatic soil treatment is supported. Final does not equate ponding with compaction or prescribe ripping, amendment, equipment or tests.
sources.applicability_limits: Generic source cannot establish contact with this garden, its soil, damage or an appropriate remedy. The under-revision banner is not carried in the candidate map; no final remediation depends on that omission.

sources.title: Evaluating Green Infrastructure Stormwater Capture Performance under Extreme Precipitation
sources.publisher: Drexel author publication record; Journal of Extreme Events / World Scientific
sources.type_and_domain: official primary guidance or primary research record; urban stormwater/bioretention
sources.reviewer_operation: independent retrieval and substantive inspection of specified governing passages; no field work or source-data reanalysis
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_units_exce: One Queens facility monitored 2011–14, sandy in-situ soils, dimensionless 3.8:1 hydraulic loading ratio. Nearly all runoff received through the inlet infiltrated there; bypass limited capture. Duration, total rain and peak-hourly intensity were associated with capture; maintenance/vegetation inference was anecdotal and future work.
sources.checked_claim_and_assessment: Final accurately limits the finding to capture versus infiltration and covariate logging. It transfers no capture percentage, overflow volume, infiltration rate or causal maintenance effect.
sources.applicability_limits: Full article/data not independently reanalyzed. Abstract formula placeholders prevent checking exact sample sizes/p-value; final makes no such numeric claim. Facility also received some runoff from outside designed tributary area, another transfer limitation.

sources.title: Water balance monitoring for two bioretention gardens in Omaha, Nebraska, 2011–14
sources.type_and_domain: official primary guidance or primary research record; urban stormwater/bioretention
sources.reviewer_operation: independent retrieval and substantive inspection of specified governing passages; no field work or source-data reanalysis
sources.locator: Official PDF report p. 9 (flume limitation), p. 13 “Performance on an Event Basis”, especially local pdftotext lines 620–631 and 809–876.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_units_exce: At DCHC, >0.7-ft ponding inundated the Parshall flume, invalidating its inflow relation and excluding large events. The two similar-depth storms differ in duration, maximum intensity and antecedent dry interval; that comparison does not isolate a causal variable. ENOA recorded no overflow during the monitoring period.
sources.checked_claim_and_assessment: Reviewer independently verified the detailed event pair the later candidate stages could not reopen. The investigator’s qualitative event-variation claim and exclusion caveat are supported; final correctly labels its own limited recheck and transfers no number.
sources.applicability_limits: Site-specific, instrument-limited observational evidence. The 0.7-ft limit is an analysis/instrument limit, not an infiltration or compliance criterion for the hypothetical garden. Reviewer retrieval does not retroactively change candidate executed work.

axes.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axes.rationale: The final is a qualified-partner research proposal, maintains four outcomes, useful alternatives, specified covariates, history inquiry, transfer limits and later observations. Negative constraints are respected. Every exact plan sentence/bullet is mapped below. Site history and owner permissions/priority are legitimate external unknowns, not missing fabricated work. Literal full-duration use is unmet and reported separately, not waived by the corrected final label.
limits: T-01 original duration unmet; separate time/scope result

axes.name: Consequential source claims and exact applicability
axes.rationale: Independent primary retrieval supports final conditional capture, inlet debris/grade, soil/underdrain, antecedent/storm and intended-bypass distinctions. Local thresholds, values and causes are not asserted. 48 hours remains contextual; Queens capture is of received water versus tributary-area capture, not a local performance promise. USGS event examples independently checked by reviewer. Earlier study-count/attribution slips do not survive as consequential final claims.
limits: No article data reanalysis; live revision IDs unavailable

axes.name: Useful unfamiliar discovery, alternatives, history and opportunity breadth
axes.rationale: Discovery yields non-obvious distinctions and actual analogous evidence: capture can fail despite infiltration; intended offline bypass; inlet orientation/divots; pretreatment maintenance; underdrain paths; Portland/New York iterative inlet history; contrasting USGS studies and visual versus quantitative assessment. Competing entry/routing, maintenance/soil and observation-first routes have meaningful decision roles. Conditional accepted bypass and qualified diagnostics avoid a preselected repair.
limits: L-03 concrete municipal histories compressed in final; supported meaning and map remain

axes.name: Wrong criticism, corrections, rejections and exact plan dispositions
axes.rationale: CR-01 correctly rejects the fulfilled-duration label, CR-02 corrects sumps typo, CR-03 appropriately retains genuinely unavailable site inputs. All three final dispositions are defensible; no criticism forces scope reduction or an unauthorized repair. No correction to hypothetical brief facts is warranted. Table assertions about generation and untimed-photo coverage are stronger than prose depth and are recorded as nonmaterial limits.
limits: Time criticism does not itself establish a scientific source defect
CR-01 correction cannot recover elapsed time

axes.name: Supported meaning preserved across discovery, draft, critique and final
axes.rationale: Four outcomes, conditional alternatives, source/site conditions, records requests, owner choices, event design, uncertainty, no-test/no-design boundaries and validation status survive in self-contained final prose. Reviser namespaces preserve S/C IDs and access limitations. Specific municipal history details are compressed, while the resulting capture/safety/maintenance tradeoff remains. Final avoids rather than repeats earlier framework attribution and Madison total-count imprecision.
limits: L-03 reduced final detail on named public inlet sequences
Candidate USGS independent recheck remained limited; reviewer check is separate

axes.name: Proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
axes.rationale: Proposed 6–10-event exploratory observations, representative interval rain, fixed views/references, separate outcomes, exact check times/misses, maintenance-period comparisons and stop/escalation are meaningful. They discriminate approach/entry from retention/outlet families, not infiltration rate, causal compaction, volume, pollutant or compliance. No numerical pass/fail performance oracle is asserted. Executed work is bounded source/document review; field, model, test and local-history verification remain unperformed.
limits: Exploratory count/times are proposals, not power or validated monitoring sufficiency
Causal attribution needs further approved measurement/control; final acknowledges this

limitations.finding: Runoff generation is represented mainly by contributing area/loading, rain and approach-flow questions. The final’s claim to preserve a complete generation account is stronger than its explanation of surface-cover/connectivity and initial losses.
limitations.why_not_material: No volume or runoff coefficient is calculated, and direct approach/entry observation plus records/survey is a viable first discriminator. Other mechanism families and unknown source area are explicit. This does not justify inventing a local runoff model obligation.

limitations.finding: The exact caveat about untimed historical ponding photographs is asserted in the plan-disposition table but developed mainly implicitly through dated records, time-stamped photos and event input logs.
limitations.why_not_material: No scientific inference relies on an untimed photograph; required later timing and input context are concrete.

validation_oracles.question: Approach/entry capture versus post-entry retention
validation_oracles.proposed_oracle: Observe approach flow reaching opening and classify enters/bypasses/both, together with ponding and recession at exact times. No approach flow must remain unknown for capture efficiency.
validation_oracles.limits: Categorical behavior narrows mechanism families, not capture volume or design failure.

validation_oracles.question: Storage/drawdown/media/outlet mechanism
validation_oracles.proposed_oracle: Confirm entry, log level/footprint and visible outlet/overflow with subsequent checks, and compare to confirmed design/local criterion.
validation_oracles.limits: Recession is not a native-soil infiltration-rate test; input/outlet/media data needed for diagnosis.

validation_oracles.question: Event/maintenance variation
validation_oracles.proposed_oracle: Exploratory 6–10 safely observable storms, representative interval rain, contrasting intensity/duration and antecedent proxy, before/after maintenance periods with confounding logged.
validation_oracles.limits: No powered inference, causal cleaning effect or exhaustive storm-class coverage promised.

validation_oracles.question: Unsafe/downstream or persistent-ponding trigger
validation_oracles.proposed_oracle: Stop unsafe/unapproved observations; notify partner for blockage, scour/settlement, road/access/property water or ponding beyond confirmed local/design criterion.
validation_oracles.limits: Not a compliance or flood-protection oracle; 48 hours is a suggested check time.

validation_oracles.question: Source/document review
validation_oracles.proposed_oracle: Candidate public-source maps plus exact discovery/plan reveal, draft, critique and final; independent reviewer primary-source corroboration.
validation_oracles.status: CANDIDATE REPORTED EXECUTED; REVIEWER INDEPENDENT SOURCE CHECKS EXECUTED
validation_oracles.limits: No archived full candidate tool trace; reviewer confirms resulting claim support, not candidate retrieval provenance.

validation_oracles.question: Local data/model/test validation
validation_oracles.proposed_oracle: Survey, site/maintenance records, rainfall analysis, instrumented water balance, infiltration/media tests, interventions or pollutant/benefit/compliance measurement.
validation_oracles.status: NOT EXECUTED; SOME FOLLOW-UP CONDITIONAL, NO IN-SCOPE INFILTRATION TEST
validation_oracles.limits: Synthetic site and explicit boundaries make such validation unavailable; no additional deployment obligation invented.
